podcast.title: Alt Rock Success and Fanbase
podcast.body: The Call, originating from Santa Cruz, California, achieved success in the Alt Rock genre throughout the 1980s and 90s, releasing nine studio albums. The band was admired by artists like U2 and Peter Gabriel. "The call had some success in the Alt Rock world through the 1980s and 90s with nine studio albums. You too and Peter Gabriel were big fans."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Reunions with Robert Been
podcast.body: Following Michael Been's death, there have been Call reunions where his son, Robert Been, filled in for his father. "Since then, there have been some call reunions during which Robert filled in for Dad."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Follow-Up Attempt for Hit (1994)
xref.body: Elden Hoke further claimed that in March 1994, Courtney Love called the Rockshop, looking to give him "the word to go ahead" with the alleged murder plot. However, Hoke was on tour at the time and missed the call, preventing them from connecting again. "Courtney until March 1994 when she allegedly called the store looking to give Elle the word to go ahead."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Psychic Hotline Call (1995)
xref.body: At 10 AM on October 21st, after having something to eat at Smoothie King on Canal Street, Shannon Hoon reportedly spent 45 minutes talking to someone on a psychic hotline. After the call, instead of joining his bandmates at the hotel, he returned to the band's bus. "While he was there, he apparently spent 45 minutes talking to somebody on a psychic hotline."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Midnight Phone Calls (Spring 2006)
xref.body: Chester began receiving late-night phone calls on his mobile, typically between 4:00 AM and 4:30 AM, but no one would speak when he answered. Upon checking the caller ID and calling the number back, he reached a switchboard operator in New Mexico who could not trace the origin of the call, leading to Chester's frustration. "Chester's mobile would bring in the middle of the night, usually between 4 and 4 30 AM, but when he answered it, no one was there."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Uncharted "Sneak Peak" - Episode 7: The Linkin Park Cyberstalker

xref.title: Attempt to Replace Singer Holly Johnson
xref.body: Following internal strife, Liverpool singer Pete Wylie was secretly approached and asked if he would like to replace Holly Johnson as the band's new singer, but Wylie declined the offer. "Then a Liverpool singer named Pete Wiley was secretly called. The call went something like this. Hey, you know what? We're sick of Holly. Would you like to be our new singer? But Pete said, no, I don't want anything to do with this."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Reunions: Some Lasted....and Sadly, Some Didn't ｜ Part 3

xref.title: Beyond The Call
xref.body: In addition to being the head of The Call, Michael Been was a composer of music for films and a hired gun for other performers. "And beyond the call, he was a composer of music for films and a hired gun for other performers."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dave Grohl's Entrance – A Desperate Call
xref.body: After his band Scream broke up mid-tour in September 1990, Dave Grohl was stranded in Los Angeles and desperate for a gig. He called his friend Buzz Osborne of The Melvins, hoping for news of drummer openings. Osborne gave Grohl Kurt Cobain's phone number, leading to an invitation to Seattle. Grohl packed his drums in a cardboard box and joined Nirvana. "So buzz gave Dave the bass player his phone number and Dave made the call and was invited to come on up Packed all his drums into a big cardboard box grabbed his only bag close and headed up the coast to join this weird little band called of course Nirvana."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Formation and Continuity
xref.body: Black Rebel Motorcycle Club was formed in 1998 by Robert Been and continues to be an active group today. Robert Been initially used the name Robert Turner to distance himself from his father's musical legacy, Michael Been of The Call. "His break came with a band called Black Rebel Motorcycle Club, a great group formed in 1998 and one that continues today."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Gray Daze Frustration
xref.body: Despite Gray Daze being a local sensation in Phoenix, releasing two indie albums ("Wake Me" in 1994 and "No Sun Today" in 1997) and opening for international acts, they failed to attract major record labels. Burned out and discouraged, Chester quit the group in 1998, contemplating giving up music altogether, until he received the call to audition for Hybrid Theory. "So burned out and discouraged, Chester quit the group in 1998, and thought about giving up music called together."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Last Phone Call with Wife
xref.body: During his last phone call with his wife, Vicki, Chris Cornell sounded groggy and slurred his words but assured her he was "fine" and "just tired." Shortly before the call, his bodyguard, Martin Kirsten, had helped him with his computer and given him two Ad-Avan tablets, a prescription for anxiety and insomnia. Vicki remained concerned after the call and asked Kirsten to check on him. "He sounded groggy and was slurring his voice, but said, no, I'm fine. I'm just tired."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
